title: Contributing to the RaukR Awesome Website 🪨
text:
Welcome! This repo exists so you can practise the GitHub workflow by contributing to a real, live website. Follow the steps below. If you get stuck, that’s expected — getting unstuck is the workshop.

💡 The golden rule: keep your content short and fun. The point is the git workflow, not writing essays.






Click Fork (top-right on GitHub). You now have your own copy at https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/raukr-awesome-website.



git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/raukr-awesome-website.git
cd raukr-awesome-website



git remote add upstream https://github.com/ninanorgren/raukr-awesome-website.git
You now have two remotes: origin (your fork) and upstream (the class repo).



Never work directly on main. Make a branch named after what you’re doing:
git switch -c add-my-profile



Pick a task (see below) and edit the files. Save.



git add .
git commit -m "Add my profile to participants"



Before you push, grab everyone else’s changes:
git pull upstream main
If you edited a shared page, this is where a merge conflict may appear. 😈 See Resolving merge conflicts below.



git push origin add-my-profile



Go to your fork on GitHub. Click Compare & pull request. Make sure it’s pointing at ninanorgren/raukr-awesome-website main. Write a short description and submit. 🎉



Nina (or a classmate) reviews your PR. If changes are requested, edit, commit, and push again to the same branch — the PR updates automatically.

🔴 Conflict likely



Start with your profile for an easy win, then try a shared page to meet your first merge conflict.




When git pull upstream main reports a conflict, Git marks the clashing lines like this:
<<<<<<< HEAD
| Your row |
=======
| A classmate's row |
>>>>>>> upstream/main
To resolve it: open the file, delete the <<<<<<<, =======, and >>>>>>> marker lines, and arrange the content so both rows are kept (this site is additive — we almost never want to throw anyone’s entry away). Then:
git add the-file-you-fixed.qmd
git commit            # finishes the merge
git push origin add-my-profile
That’s it — you’ve resolved a merge conflict. 🏆




You don’t need this to contribute — you only edit Markdown — but if you have Quarto installed:
quarto preview
Otherwise, just open your PR: the site rebuilds and deploys automatically once your change is merged.

title: Welcome to the RaukR 2026 Awesome Website 🪨
text:
🎯 Your mission
By the end of the workshop you should have:

Forked this repository to your own GitHub account.
Added yourself to the Participants gallery.
Made at least one contribution to a shared page (and survived the resulting merge conflict 😈).
Opened a pull request back to this repo and gotten it merged.







TipBrand new? Start here



Head straight to the Contributing guide. It walks you through fork → clone → branch → commit → push → PR, step by step.

title: ✨ R One-Liners
text:
The Collection
Maria — count rows per group without dplyr:
table(df$species)
Johan — the entire tidyverse in one breath:
df |> group_by(g) |> summarise(m = mean(x), .groups = "drop")
Martín — Tells you when it’s time to leave the lab
Sys.time()
Ale — lapply instead of for loops
list –> lapply(list, function(x) x^2)
Mohito — Prints my name
print(rev(rev(rev(rev(rev(c("Jag" ,"heter", "Mohit")))))))

title: 📚 Recommendations

The List

📄 Paper — “Tidy Data” (Wickham, 2014) — Maria — will change how you store data forever.
🎧 Podcast — Not So Standard Deviations — Johan — stats chat that doesn’t put you to sleep.
